source.title: Minimum Lights to Illuminate a Road

teaching.hint: At the leftmost unlit position, which placement could serve it while helping farthest to the right?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Existing large intervals can be aggregated once; the first remaining dark position forces a new bulb, and shifting it right maximizes useful future coverage.
solution_outline.approach: Mark existing bulbs’ coverage using interval range updates. Scan positions in order; at the first uncovered position, add a new bulb as far right as possible while still covering it, then skip its illuminated positions.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before each scan point, all earlier positions are covered. A chosen bulb covers the first dark point and reaches at least as far right as any competing bulb that could cover it.
solution_outline.correctness: Every solution needs a new bulb covering the first dark position. Moving such a bulb to the rightmost legal location loses no coverage that still matters; repeat by exchange over successive dark positions.
solution_outline.pitfall: At the last road position, the nominal `p+1` location is outside the road; place the bulb at `p` instead.

common_wrong_turns: Painting each existing bulb interval cell by cell
Placing each new bulb exactly at the first dark point
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained inclusive clipped intervals and permission to install at any road position.
